a date with no offset is read as UTC — 08:00 is 08:00Z in UTC (v2; row D16)
because: feed.ts toISODate — a zoneless date takes `Z` (an ISO date-time) or ` GMT`; ruled 2026-10-05 (P107-D16, "UTC, and no date if unknown"); the same steps in Paris below

name: … and the same feed in Europe/Paris is 08:00Z too: one feed, one Published, wherever it is parsed (v2; was row D16: 06:00Z here)
because: feed.ts toISODate — a zoneless ISO date-time is local time in ECMAScript, so the reader adds `Z` before `Date.parse` reads it

name: a zone name Date.parse does not know gives no date: 08:00 CEST is published as null, not 08:00Z; EST is understood (v2; was row D16: CEST read as UTC, two hours late)
because: feed.ts toISODate — a trailing zone name outside the twelve V8 reads (UT, UTC, GMT, Z and the eight US names) gives null; v1's retry replaced it with ' UTC'

name: a feed that does not say when it changed sends Feed Updated as empty text, clearing the previous feed's date, as every other Feed output does (v3; was row D17: '|| undefined' was never sent)
